lesson.scenario: A limiter estimates a trailing 60-second count from the previous and current fixed-window counters.
entities: Reports window id and elapsed fraction
Stores admissions in the active window
Compares the estimate with limit seven

steps.title: Prior window closes
steps.narration: Window 200 ends with eight admitted requests recorded for interpolation.
steps.outcome: The exact prior total becomes the decaying history term.
steps.invariant: Rotation must atomically preserve the completed count and clear the new current bucket.

steps.title: History begins decaying
steps.narration: At four seconds into window 201, the prior count has weight 56/60.
steps.outcome: The recent burst still fills the estimated trailing window.
steps.invariant: The historical contribution decreases continuously rather than resetting at a boundary.

steps.title: Decay permits an admission
steps.narration: At sixteen seconds, weighted history is 5.87, so the projected count 6.87 admits one request.
steps.invariant: The estimator uses the count before the candidate request, then increments only on admission.

steps.title: Current traffic fills estimate
steps.narration: At thirty seconds, two more requests project counts six and seven, raising the current counter to three.
steps.outcome: The combined weighted history and active count reaches the limit.
steps.invariant: Both counters for one key must be read and updated under a consistent rotation epoch.

steps.title: At-limit request rejected
steps.narration: A request one tenth of a second later projects 7.99 and leaves the current count unchanged.
steps.outcome: The candidate would push the estimate above seven.
steps.invariant: Admission compares the projected count, not merely the stored current counter.

steps.title: Further decay reopens capacity
steps.narration: At thirty-eight seconds, the projected count falls to 6.93 and one more request is admitted.
steps.outcome: Admission capacity changes smoothly as historical traffic ages out.
steps.invariant: The two-counter approximation bounds storage but is not an exact timestamp log.

production.scenario: A partner sync API accepts CRM contact upserts from thousands of tenant daemons and uses an approximate sliding-window counter to cap each app at 20,000 requests per 15 minutes across the edge fleet.
components: pushes contact upsert batches from tenant systems
owns inbound upsert intake at the public edge
approximates rolling usage for each partner app key
authoritative sink for admitted upsert work
stores shard checkpoints consumed by replacement edge pods in other regions
stores throttled-request evidence for billing and partner support tooling
flows: A tenant daemon sends a large contact sync burst after an overnight export job.
fetch tenant beta rolling quota plan rev 88
The API loads the 20k per 15-minute rolling contract for the calling app.
apply weighted-window plan for app beta-crm
The counter service receives the current policy and approximation weights before admission.
evaluate app beta-crm in rolling interval 14:00-14:15
The request is checked against the approximate trailing usage shared by many edge pods.
enqueue admitted batch CT-8801 to crm.upsert.ingest
Accepted batches become durable queue work for the materializer fleet.
Shard state is checkpointed so an edge replacement can resume from the latest snapshot.
emit throttle record for app beta-crm
Approximation-based rejects are preserved for billing support and replay workflows.
